note.note:
Consult Summary:
- New, constant severe headache for 3 days with photophobia and transient “shooting lights” in a woman on a combined oral contraceptive; working impression is probable migraine with aura (persistent), with consideration of secondary causes (e.g., cerebral venous sinus thrombosis) given new-onset severity and OCP use. Plan: start stronger NSAID plus acetaminophen, arrange in-person neuro and funduscopic exam, check blood pressure, safety net to ED if worsening.

History:
- Presenting complaint/timeline: Sudden-onset “blinding” headache on awakening 3 days ago; continuous since. Severity up to 8/10, decreases to ~5/10 with ibuprofen but never resolves. Diffuse, worse over right eye.
- Associated symptoms: Photophobia; transient visual phenomena (“shooting lights,” “weird vision”); mild nausea without vomiting. Sleep intact (not waking at night) but wakes with headache. Brief stabbing pain with standing quickly; sensation of “something moving” with abrupt head movement. No focal neurologic symptoms (no numbness, tingling, weakness). No change in smell or taste. No URI/sinus symptoms, cough, feverish feeling, epistaxis, or hemoptysis. Reports reduced energy likely secondary to headache.
- Pertinent negatives: No prior similar prolonged headaches; past headaches brief and relieved by ibuprofen. No recent travel.
- Past medical history: No chronic conditions reported; remote unspecified pain in youth, resolved.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Medications: Combined oral contraceptive (“the pill”) started ~1 year ago; intermittent ibuprofen for headache. No other regular meds.
- Social: Lives alone; works from home, missed/limited work due to headache. Non-smoker. Alcohol about once weekly (~3 drinks). No recreational drug use.
- Family history: Mother with severe migraines including vomiting.
- Preventive/monitoring: Blood pressure reportedly normal at pharmacy a year ago; recent optometry exam “normal” per patient.

Examination:
- No in-person exam performed during teleconsult.
- Vitals: Not obtained.
- Reported/observed: None. Patient reports recent optometry exam with no change in vision.

Impression:
- Working diagnosis: Migraine with aura, persistent (possible status migrainosus) given severe continuous headache, photophobia, positive visual phenomena, unilateral peri-orbital emphasis, mild nausea, family history, and partial NSAID response.
- Differential (top 2–3):
  1) Migraine with aura (high likelihood) — supported by photophobia, visual phenomena, severity, right supraorbital predominance, family history, partial response to NSAID.
  2) Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (medium likelihood) — new persistent severe headache in a woman on a combined OCP; some positional sensitivity. No focal deficits or papilledema reported, but warrants consideration until examined.
  3) Tension-type headache (low–medium) — constant diffuse pain could fit, but severity, photophobia, and visual phenomena are less typical.

Plan:
- Medications: Prescribe a stronger NSAID alternative to ibuprofen; may take with acetaminophen concurrently. Take with food.
- In-person assessment: Book clinic visit for full neurologic examination and funduscopic exam (to assess for papilledema) and check blood pressure.
- Contraception counseling: If migraine with aura is confirmed, discuss changing from combined oral contraceptive to a non-estrogen option; continue current pill for now per clinician’s guidance.
- Safety net: If headache becomes unbearable, worsens, or changes character (e.g., new neurologic symptoms, thunderclap onset, persistent vomiting, fever, confusion, vision loss), go to the emergency department. Patient may call clinic for further advice.
- Work/functional: Patient currently working from home with reduced capacity; reassess after treatment and exam.
- Follow-up: Proceed with scheduled in-person appointment; cancel if symptoms fully resolve beforehand per discussion.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: No vitals (including current blood pressure), no in-person neurologic or funduscopic findings, exact OCP name/dose not recorded, no pain triggers/relievers beyond NSAIDs, no pregnancy status documented.  
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None material; DDx adds consideration of CVST not explicitly discussed in the visit but consistent with context (OCP use and new severe headache).  
● Transcript quality: Several inaudible/redacted segments (patient identifiers and OCP name), limiting specificity; otherwise coherent history with some ambiguity regarding alcohol quantity.
